historical_references.reference: The Tamangs, also known as the Bhotias or the Lhobpas, are a Tibetan Buddhist people who inhabit the highlands north of the Himalayas in Nepal and Bhutan. They are believed to have originated from Tibet and migrated to this region during the 12th and 13th centuries.

The Tamangs are also known for their distinct cultural practices, including their unique system of polyandry, where a man can marry multiple wives living in separate houses. This practice is believed to have been influenced by the local climate and geography, which makes it difficult for men to farm the land and support multiple families in a single household.
